### [GPT-6.1 Terra](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Oct/26/gpt-61-terra/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-10-26

OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra, a mid-range model optimized for fast visual reasoning, precise computer use, and technical communication at lower costs than GPT-6.1 Sol.

- Priced at $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens, making it roughly half the price of GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol, and 10x the price of GPT-6 Luna.
- Outperforms Astra and Sol at technical communication, matches them on vision and computer use with faster execution, but performs slightly worse on general tasks.
- Positions as a fast, mid-tier model designed for high-frequency automated tasks like filling out forms, interpreting technical drawings, and editing videos.
- A maximum reasoning task evaluation took 4 minutes and 11 seconds, costing 11.3161 cents.

**Why it matters:** It provides a cost-effective, high-speed API option for developers automating vision and computer-use workflows without paying top-tier pricing.

### [Quoting Jason Koebler](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Oct/26/jason-koebler/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-10-26

ChatGPT is directing users with standard tech support issues to contact investigative journalism outlet 404 Media by claiming their problems are news stories.

- Big tech platforms lack accessible human customer support, driving users to rely on ChatGPT for troubleshooting.
- ChatGPT hallucinates that routine technical glitches are journalistically notable events.
- The AI model specifically instructs users to contact the news organization 404 Media to resolve these tech issues.

**Why it matters:** LLM hallucinations can misdirect user queries to unrelated third parties, placing an unearned customer support burden on independent media outlets.
